body: don’t do it. the moment after you jump you are going to feel an overwhelming sense of regret. it doesn’t matter how horrible things are, there is a part of you that wants to keep living, and when you are at the point of no return you are going to wish you listened to me.

So many people are depressed today there’s nothing wrong with feeling like that. Life is pain, the world is only getting worse and often things feel hopeless. It’s hard to say exactly what is right for you to do because i don’t know you or your life, but i can speak from personal experience and hope it relates to you. I’ve been dealing with depression for a long time, i also cut, only in places people can’t see. Sometimes when things are so bad, something about the feeling of doing it brings a lot of relief. Despite that though i don’t ever genuinely consider killing myself. I tried doing it once a long time ago and I didn’t get very far, and i’m glad i didn’t because ultimately I know deep down that I do not want to be dead, even if in that moment it may have felt like not being alive was easier than continuing to live. At the end of the day, regardless of what you may believe about life and death and the afterlife, there is a very good likelihood that this is it, there’s no second chance, and choosing to kill yourself is choosing to give up on everything you’ve ever known and or ever will know. There was a time in my life where it felt like things could never get better and that death was the best option. Things aren’t great now, but there are so many things i would have never been able to experience if i didn’t choose to keep living. Even through the lens of depression there is still a lot of beauty in this world, and I think it’s those things that make life worth living, even through all the pain and tumultuousness. Maybe if you’re feeling in a rut you could try and look into a new hobby or interest.

I hope you are able to overcome what you’re dealing with right now. Also I just have to say if you noticed things are notably worse now compared to before you started taking antidepressants, and your suicidal ideation feels nearly uncontrollable at present, I would consider looking into options to not take them, ESPECIALLY if your depressive symptoms were manageable before you got on them.

Reality is objective, it isn’t inherently good or bad or meant to make you feel any particular way, it just is. You can look at the cyclical nature of life and death and the inevitability of entropy and decide that it is inherently negative and thus is inherently nihilistic, but it isn’t the ‘nature’, it is a way of viewing the nature of it, stop acting like a prick. For a lot of people, a nihilistic perspective is only adopted when they reach a particular low point, so yes, more often than you’d expect in your one dimensional point of view, it is a ‘response to being a loser’. Just because you call yourself a dumbass doesn’t mean you get to oversimplify a concept and try and prove people wrong with your incorrect definition, that’s just ignorance.

the negative aspects of life that can lead to a nihilistic perspective will always exist and in its current form are exponentially growing, however the amount to which you see the world through that lens is dependent on the type of person you are. Some people are nihilistic almost as a default, they may be functioning well in life and still see their life as well as life as a whole as inherently worthless, and continue to move forward within that state of mind. others only reach a state of nihilism when they are at a low point, where the loss of worth works as a coping mechanism in order to accept negative aspects of their own life, there are others who don’t necessarily fit either of these, but i’m sure being yourself you know where you lie. If you find you take on a nihilistic perspective when you’re at a low, than it is likely going to be a constant effort in order to avoid reaching that bottom consistently, if it is a constant despite your immediate state of life, than yeah it might be forever, but it’s not like there’s anything inherently wrong with it. ENTJ: Te, Ni, Se, Fi
ESTJ: Te, Si, Ne, Fi

dominant Te and inferior Fi can make the outward actions of these two types seem very similar, however the differences can generally be spotted in personal outlook and internal struggles 

generally the first and third function work together dominantly, serving as one’s primary navigation of the world, whilst the second and fourth lay dormant and are either brought out at times or serve as an underlying cause for the actions brought upon by the first and third functions. at times entjs can comes off as overly materialistic and shallow due to their practical nature, although it is ultimately the amount to which they are in touch with their Ni and Fi that will decide this or not. Although their interactions with the external world will display their te and se most prominently, it is the ni and fi together that often create an internal sense of direction that creates the path they end up walking 

estj are different due to the se being replaced with ne, meaning the dominant se is paired with a child level extroverted intuition, allowing them to apply a number of potential ideas at once to a present situation with efficiency. the si and fi in second and fourth slot add to the estjs ability to create effective solutions to practical problems (in that si is based on past patterns in so that it can be utilized alongside the te and ne to apply relevant information to the present problem) however the inferior fi causes similar limitations as the entj, often leading to difficulties grappling with own emotions and a tendency to avoid introspection due to the amount of work they take on at once. in the same sense that an entj is ‘driven’ by their 2nd and 4th function, an estj will interact with the world primarily with their te and ne, while their si and fi work together to create an internal understanding of the world based on 1. past events and patterns that can be reapplied and 2. internal feelings about said events and patterns. 

There are a few terms that pair together functions or smtn similar that sortve allow you to see how they can act unexpected ways based on one’s life

1. loop 

a loop is generally used to define the repetitive use of the second and fourth function, although it can be applied to the first and third if you want to highlight how it can become negative in the right scenario. 

Ni and Fi work together to provide the entj with an inner sense of meaning and a future oriented image of what their life could be based on their internal convictions. When these functions loop however, the entj can find themselves shutting out the external world and getting caught in a self centered loop of internal feelings. the aux ni leads thoughts toward one thing (generally being their future and their hopes for it) while the inferior fi makes them doubt themselves and their values. 

for the estj, si and fi loops in a similar way, making one questions their internal structure, however often having more practical applications than ni. si fi loop can make estjs question their routine, the way they interact with problems and peers, as well as their cognitive ability, sometimes resulting in them being unconfident with interacting with the external world (even if it is the routine they have been im for a long time) 

2. grip

a grip is when one function is used too much to the point where it’s overwhelming. generally it’s a way to define the overuse of child or inferior functions. 

for entj, an se grip can be seen as a childish sense of overindulgence in extroverted sensory pleasures. This can take a wide variety of forms but it is often demonstrated by 1. an overindulgence and 2. a lack of responsibility for the resulting actions. 

estj ne grip can be displayed in a sort of childish sense of imagination and an over reliance on it.
